## Active

### D-028 — The mongodb adapter adds a string id to every document

> _2026-08-23 · core/blong-gogo · active_

Mongo `_id` is an ObjectId, which scalar flattening drops, so the commander had no unique label or
key for a row. The adapter's `{...doc, id: String(_id)}` is an intentional, small contract change;
the CRUD test mask and the mongodb tap snapshots were updated to match. Tap snapshots are
order-sensitive, so `id` has to be the LAST field of the projected document.

### D-043 — A later validation file replaces an earlier one for the same method

> _2026-08-18 · core/blong-gogo · active_

`Registry._validations()` now replaces a later-registered validation per `methodParts` key — the
plan's primary option — instead of adding an explicit `override` flag on gateway files. Replacement
is minimal and deterministic, and it also fixes the ut-function.merge TypeBox `Kind`-symbol
corruption where nested `details` arrays threw "Unknown type". No existing code relied on same-key
merging.

### D-044 — $subject/$object placeholders are resolved by the framework

> _2026-08-18 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The kopi template's `$subject`/`$object` placeholder names are valid identifiers everywhere they
appear, so a scaffold-time content rewrite was rejected and the fix is framework-side. `methodParts`
in `lib.ts` and `capitalize` (four call sites) became `$`-aware, which makes the derived names
consistent with the `$subject$Object...` file names. This is the "stripping/absorbing the `$` at the
proper places" that was asked for.

### D-045 — The graceful-shutdown timer bounds the stop, not the run

> _2026-08-18 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The 30-second timer was moved from handler creation into the signal handler. Left where it was, it
self-destructed any long-running `blong`/`blong-watch` server 30 seconds after start — the root
cause of the Playwright webServer backend dying mid-run.

### D-046 — `remove` deletes FK-constrained detail rows before the master

> _2026-08-18 · core/blong-gogo · active_

A master with children could not be deleted because the foreign key was non-cascading. The generic
`remove` now deletes FK-constrained detail rows first, which is consistent with `edit` replacing its
children.

### D-047 — Three framework warnings turn silent stalls into named methods

> _2026-08-18 · core/blong-gogo · active_

Permanent, intent-agnostic diagnostics that gate themselves on trouble: `Registry._matchMethods`
warns when a handler factory exceeds 3 seconds and names the method; `Remote` warns when a
`canSkipSocket` lookup finds no local method; and `blong-server/subject.ts` warns when a derived
model handler name matches no registered file, naming the closest match. These would have pinpointed
the `$`-mismatch hang and the `_validations()` stall immediately instead of after an investigation.

### D-048 — The gogo-kopi cycle is broken by moving createRealm into gogo

> _2026-08-21 · core/blong-gogo · active_

`blong-kopi` must stay a runnable, testable realm — its `index.test.ts` loads `blong-gogo`, and it
demonstrates RBAC through `blong-access` — so the cycle had to break elsewhere. The root cause was a
`gogo`/`kopi` two-cycle plus access: `gogo.deps → blong-kopi` (scaffolder re-export),
`kopi.devDeps → gogo`, `kopi.devDeps → access`, `access.devDeps → gogo`, introduced when kopi gained
its framework devDependencies. The chosen fix (option 1) dropped `gogo → kopi`: `blong-gogo` now
owns `createRealm` (`src/kopi.ts`, moved from `blong-kopi/kopi.ts`) and resolves the template from
either the monorepo sibling `core/blong-kopi` or a publish-bundled `template/` generated ONLY at
publish time by `scripts/copy-template.mjs` (gitignored, shipped through gogo's `.npmignore`). gogo
is a sink; `blong-dev`/`blong-kopi`/`access` form a chain with no back-edge, `rush update` succeeds,
kopi tap is 6/6 and blong-gogo 259 pass. The `blong-kopi/kopi.ts` twin kept at the time for direct
use was later deleted because it had ZERO consumers (the CLI's `bin/blong.ts` and the runtime's
`load.ts` both import gogo's `src/kopi.ts`), and the template file enumeration moved into a shared
`core/blong-gogo/src/template-files.ts` (`TEMPLATE_FILES_IGNORE` plus `listTemplateFiles`) used by
both `src/kopi.ts` and `scripts/copy-template.mjs`, so the two can no longer drift.

### D-049 — Resource-backed CRUD and graph edges are opt-in in the knex exec

> _2026-08-19 · core/blong-gogo · active_

blong-access had about 18 `adapter/db` handlers that only did resource-backed CRUD
(`coreResourceEnsure` on add, a name join on find/get, resource rename on edit, cascade on remove,
and `core_triple` `hasRole`/`hasCapability`/`hasAction` edge sync), so the built-in knex `exec`
absorbs them, opt-in via `ISchemaTable.resource: true` and `ISchemaTable.edges[]`. `add` generates
server-side PKs for `uuid`/`ulid` default markers and for resource-backed not-null PKs (FK to
`core.resource`, no default, PK absent), creates `core_type` plus `core_resource`, strips the
virtual `${object}Name` from the insert and joins the name onto the result; `find`/`get` join the
name, `edit` renames the resource, and `remove` cascades entity row to resource row plus the
declared edges (including `reverse` bindings). Because it is opt-in, realms that declare nothing are
unaffected; role CRUD is now fully generic (10 handlers deleted) while the user and capability
handlers stay custom. `exec` also gained `ulid` handling, and the `uidNotNull`-PK caveat is
documented in the blong-schema skill. Fixed on the way: the remove order (FK), a reverse-only edge
binding clobbering the master key, the edge name join on Buffers, and a missing `${object}Name` on
the add result. Verified: tap 22/22, Playwright 19/19, both packages' lint.

### D-050 — The exec `get` lost its edges to an in-place row mutation

> _2026-08-19 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The new integration tests found a real bug: `get` read `masterKey = row?.[keyName]` AFTER
`prepareResultRow(row, …)` had mutated the row in place (Buffer to base64 string), so
`Buffer.isBuffer(masterKey)` was false and the declared edges were never attached. Fixed by
capturing the raw PK before the mutation. `resolveTableSpec` was also widened to accept an
`undefined` tableConfig.

### D-060 — The access audit id reaches the handler via an awaited preHandler

> _2026-08-20 · core/blong-gogo · active_

`access.audit.record` now returns `{inserted, auditIds}` with the ULID keys it generated.
`recordAccessAudit` in `core/blong-gogo/src/jwt.ts` sets the first one on
`request.auth.credentials.auditId`, and the gateway's `_meta()` spreads credentials into the
handler's `$meta.auth`, so `$meta.auth.auditId` is available to the business handler. To make the id
reliable the preHandler hook now AWAITS the audit insert where it used to fire and forget: failures
are still caught and never fail the request, but every access-checked request pays a database write
on the request path. Denied (403) requests are still audited before the error is thrown, so both
outcomes are recorded, and the id is per-request only because the credentials object is re-created —
the bearer cache is not polluted. Verified: tap access 37/37 (including the new `auditIds` ULID
assertion), gateway 20/20, party 15/15, kopi 6/6, Playwright 21 passed.

### D-061 — Transient MySQL connection loss is retried in the knex adapter

> _2026-08-21 · core/blong-gogo · active_

Intermittent `PROTOCOL_CONNECTION_LOST` (`fatal: true`) in GitHub Actions failed random packages,
one or more at a time. MySQL is a k8s Deployment in k3d (`mysql/mysql-server:8.0.32`, 768Mi,
`max_connections=151` defaults) and the knex adapter had no pool tuning, no keepalive and no retry,
so a single transient drop during schema sync or seeding was fatal. The adapter
(`core/blong-gogo/src/adapter/schema/knex/json.ts`) gained `isRetryableConnectionError` plus
`withConnectionRetry`, which re-executes builders through `clone()` and `raw()` by re-invocation
with linear backoff, gated by an explicit `knex.retry` config enabled ONLY in the `ci`/`dev` blocks
of the shared `srv.db` adapter (`core/blong-server/adapter/db.ts`) and never in prod; mysql2
`enableKeepAlive` and tarn's `pool.maxConnectionLifetimeMillis` are enabled in the same non-prod
blocks. An `onConnectionError` logging hook (`logKnexConnectionError`) reports diagnostics even when
retry is off. v1 does NOT retry whole transactions, only inner builder and raw queries, to avoid
re-running user callbacks with external side effects, and MySQL's `max_connections` and memory were
left alone until diagnostics show `ER_CON_COUNT_ERROR` (1040) or OOMKilled, because the observed
signature points to a pod restart or an idle drop rather than connection exhaustion. Verified: full
blong-gogo `tsc --noEmit` green, 89/89 tap tests including the new retry and connection-error cases,
`ci-lint` clean on the changed files.

### D-062 — The redis adapter's stop() must disconnect, not only quit

> _2026-09-07 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The redis adapter's `stop()` called `quit()` on a lazy or still-connecting ioredis client, which
left the 6379 socket open and made tap exit with `timeout!`. `adapter/server/redis.ts` now calls
`disconnect()` after `quit()` — best-effort and idempotent.

### D-101 — Introspection is data-only and optional on the registry interfaces

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · active_

`Registry.describe()` and `Watch.describe()` return plain serializable data (realms, ports, groups,
folders, files) from `IRegistry` and `IGateway` as optional methods, so existing implementations and
mocks stay valid. `Watch` gained a separate `#discoveredFiles` map rather than being asked to expose
`#handlerFiles`, because the latter drives hot-reload decisions and must not change.

### D-111 — Process lifetime became per-intent config instead of a CI check

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · active_

`runServer` now asks `platform.exit` instead of evaluating
`process.env.CI && !intents.includes('playwright')` in two places. The flag is declared per intent
in `load.ts`'s synthetic config: `integration` keeps `Boolean(process.env.CI)` so CI stays the
single source for that intent, `playwright: {exit: false}` retires the last hardcoded intent-name
string, and `db` and `cli` are `true`. It is resolved onto `IRegistry.exit` right before `load()`
returns, next to where `api.configRuntime` is attached, because the runner only ever holds the
registry and something had to carry the value across.

### D-112 — A framework intent's false survives every later source merge

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The standalone-realm wrapper's convenience ports were defeating `cli`. Rather than pattern-match
intent names, the resolved framework configs are retained and any top-level `false` they declare is
re-applied after the merge. Only `cli` sets top-level `false`s today, so the rule has no effect on
any existing intent, but it states the right invariant: an intent that switches a component off must
not be overridable by a template's defaults.

### D-113 — The cli intent disables listeners and watching, not the load

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · active_

`gateway`, `rpcServer`, `apiGateway`, `restFs`, `systemDebug`, `mcp` and `resolution` are `false`,
and `watch: {enabled: false}` is used deliberately rather than `watch: false`, because the load step
that records handler folders and files — the data behind `Registry.describe()` and therefore behind
`method.find` and `tree.find` — runs in `Watch.start` regardless; only chokidar is gated by
`enabled`. Dispatch stays in-process through `remote: {canSkipSocket: true}`. Verified by running
`blong cli` against a minimal suite: exit 0 and nothing bound, while a default run still opens the
rpc server and the gateway.

### D-114 — The CI check is a browser-safe function, not a ci intent block

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The browser bundle loads `load.ts` too, so `Boolean(process.env.CI)` threw
`ReferenceError: process is not defined` and broke the entire browser platform. The tempting fix was
to stop reading the environment and drive the flag from the `ci` intent, which `runServer.ts`
already injects, through a `ci: {exit: true}` block. That was rejected: intents are merged in
command-line order, so a `ci` block setting `exit` would override `playwright: {exit: false}`
whenever the Playwright runner adds its intent before `ci`, silently breaking Playwright in CI. The
chosen fix is `isCI()` reading `globalThis.process?.env?.['CI']` — a function, not a module
constant, so the tests that set `process.env.CI` at runtime still pass; a constant is captured at
import time and would have failed `exit.intent.test.ts` and its nine tests.

### D-115 — The cli intent currently only supports a realm-only suite

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The claim that `cli` is framework-level, so any realm or suite is drivable from a terminal, was
verified false as written: `blong-login/orchestrator/login/token.ts` reads `gateway.config()` at
handler-creation time, and `cli` sets `gateway: false`, so any suite containing the auth realm fails
to load with a `TypeError` reading `config` — reproduced in `demo/handler-test-poc`. The intent's
real contract today is "a realm-only suite", which is what Stage 4 needs: `core/blong-kukum/cli.ts`
is the kukum realm alone and `blong cli` there exits 0. If `cli` should ever work on a full suite,
fix `blong-login` to read the gateway lazily rather than weakening `cli`, because a config-only
gateway would re-open the question of which components `cli` switches off — the question the
false-wins rule exists to settle.

### D-116 — A library function's this now carries platform and registry

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · active_

`Registry._createHandlers` seeds `lib` with `error`, `assert`, `render`, `timing` and
`@feasibleone/blong-lib`, and that object is what `this` is inside a `library()` function. The plan
assumed `this` would be the port with no framework change, which was measured false: the lib proxy
hands an attached function back raw and only binds `port` in its not-yet-attached fallback path,
confirmed by a throwaway probe. Rather than accept an inconsistent `this` that works only for
not-yet-attached libraries, `platform: this.#platform` and `registry: this` were added, mirroring
the port API which already exposed both. This is what lets a library function reach the platform at
all, which the modular-CLI goal needs, since a `library()` factory is given only `config`,
`handler`, `errors`, `schema`, `gateway` and `apiSchema`. Blast radius is two additive keys on one
object, verified against the full `blong-gogo` suite and lint; the rejected alternative was passing
the platform as an explicit parameter through every binding.

### D-117 — The cli intent loads the handler-bearing layers too

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · active_

Without this, a `cli` process loaded a realm with no handler layers, because `WELL_KNOWN_LAYERS`
bound them to `integration` only, so there was nothing to dispatch to. `cli` still skips the
listeners, the watcher and the test machinery; it just no longer skips the realm. Fixing it in the
layer map rather than by passing `['cli','integration']` to `load` was deliberate: the false-wins
reconciliation forces any top-level `false` from a framework config, and `integration.exit` is
`isCI()` — false outside CI — so the extra intent would have silently cancelled `cli`'s
`exit: true`. Follow-up: the two prose tables that mirror this map, `_shared/conventions.md` under
`[LAYER_DEFAULTS_TABLE]` and `docs/concepts/layer.md`, still show `integration` only.

### D-118 — A CLI resolves its method with findHandler, not the prefix match

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · active_

`Remote` is not reachable from the registry's public surface, but `findHandler` resolves the same
entry `Remote._findMethod` would. The guard must be `findHandler` returning a function, because
`handles()` matches only the namespace prefix and answers `true` for `kukum.bogus.thing`, so it
cannot distinguish a real method. Calling the handler directly skips gateway validation and
checkpoints, which a CLI does not need: it constructs its own parameters, and kukum is
unauthenticated.

### D-119 — CLI results own stdout, and framework logs are configured down

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · active_

pino writes to fd 1 directly, so overriding `process.stdout.write` — the obvious trick — does not
catch framework logs; that was verified by trying it. Instead the `cli` path sets
`{log: {level: 'warn'}, apiSchema: {logLevel: 'warn'}}` on the suite and `{cli: {logLevel: 'warn'}}`
on the orchestrator, whose `default` block asks for `info`. `--output=json` therefore stays
parseable while real warnings still surface.

### D-139 — The CLI plumbing moved into blong-gogo, component log levels did not

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-gogo · active_

`core/blong-gogo/src/cli.ts` (exported as `@feasibleone/blong-gogo/cli.ts`) now owns what
`bin/kukum.ts` had hand-rolled: `parseArgv` and `wantsHelp`, `resolveMethod` including the
`handles()` prefix versus `findHandler()` distinction, `isCliEntry`, and `runCli`, which does help
and usage, `load(suite, name, name, ['cli'])`, start, dispatch, keeps stdout for the result while
forwarding everything else to stderr, handles `--output=json|text` with the TTY default, exit codes
and `registry.stop()` in a `finally`. `bin/kukum.ts` went from 273 to about 200 lines, almost all of
it kukum's own usage text, argument-to-method mapping and result rendering, and the new
`bin/blong-cli.ts` demo is about 90 lines. The `cli` intent block in `load.ts` also defaults
`log: {level: 'warn'}` and `apiSchema: {logLevel: 'warn'}`, so a realm no longer has to remember
them. A component's own `logLevel` was deliberately NOT moved: it lives in the component's
`activation` and the framework does not know component names, so every command-driven component
still declares `cli: {logLevel: 'warn'}` and the rule is documented in
`docs/blong/docs/patterns/cli.md` rather than changed. Verified: CLI output byte-identical to the
pre-extraction baseline, kukum 490 of 490, blong-gogo 261 pass and 6 skip.

### D-175 — ACL enforcement has two entry points and one error family

> _2026-09-16 · core/blong-gogo · active_

The generic CRUD gates get/edit/remove (403 acl.denied, 404 acl.notFound for reads so existence is
not leaked), filters find before paging and filters the auto-bound dropdown lists; add is checked
against the scope named by the tables addScope declaration. Realm handlers reach the same SQL
through the adapter port (aclCheck, aclFilter) because the runtime package is not a library
dependency of a realm. Both throw the same acl.* error names declared in the realm error map and in
the adapter error map, so a caller sees one name wherever the check runs.

### D-178 — Self-scoped tables guard records whose scope points at them

> _2026-09-16 · core/blong-gogo · active_

party.organization cannot use the forward scope form: the graph is unit --belongsTo--> organization,
so an organization has no scope edge, would count as unscoped, and would fall back to RBAC (i.e.
stay unguarded). Reverse traversal (enumerating the units that belong to it) was rejected: the scope
of an organization IS the organization, and the unit-to-org direction only says which units it owns.
acl.selfScope: true therefore makes the record its own scope - scope set = the record plus its
parent scopes through access.effectiveScope - with no unscoped fallback. Admin holds the
organization scope in the party seed, which is what makes the two seeded organizations
differentiate.

### D-181 — Wildcard ACL rule: targetKind all anchored on the access.any node

> _2026-09-16 · core/blong-gogo · active_

Approved by the user as option A. An access_acl row with targetKind all matches every record of
every guarded table, in the record and scope paths and on add; targetId points at a bare sentinel
resource named (all records) of type access.any so the foreign key and the ACL Rules page stay
uniform, and core.resource.ensure now supports a table-less bare node. A deny still wins over it.
The access realm seeds an allow-all rule for the Admin role over the guarded party actions in its
production reference data, so an administrator is never narrowed - which is also what makes a newly
created organization readable by its creator. test.acl.flow keeps its out-of-scope proofs by adding
a testViewer login (a principal with no grant) and by writing its own organization deny at runtime.

### D-223 — Call traces get their own channel, gated by config and a signed grant

> _2026-09-19 · core/blong-gogo · active_

Call-phase records (start/end/error/received) currently ride the level API: the gateway's note(),
handlerProxy.recordedCall and AdapterBase.handle all write through port.log.info, so they print
whenever the level admits info, and there is no switch of their own. Owner decisions: (1) they move
to log.calls, a channel on the log internal with phase methods and no level parameter, reached from
a port as port.log.calls - on by default everywhere, stdout off by default and opt-in via config,
with a per-flow opt-out for high-TPS flows, because the flow ledger and the diagrams are built from
these records so there is no fallback if they stop being produced; (2) the per-request capability is
x-blong-grant, a signed-only JWT with {cap, exp}; (3) the gateway verifies it once at the earliest
hook and forwards a plain marker inside meta.forward, downstream processes trust it; (4) it is
minted by a framework CLI intent (blong grant calls) so it ships with the runtime image; (5) the
second cause of the noise is fixed too - SemanticLog.child ignored options.level, so the gateway's
logLevel: warn never silenced it (Gateway.ts passes level to child), and fastify's own request
logging dumped the whole request including the Authorization bearer at info. Opt-out mechanism
concluded: by flow, decided at flow minting from config matched against the entry method, fixed for
the flow's life, carried in meta.forward so every process in the flow agrees, and checked at every
emission point so nothing of an opted-out flow is ever written. Recorded in the flow's config rather
than per call, because a per-call decision could opt out of one hop and leave the rest of a high-TPS
flow recording.

### D-224 — A realm a suite names is no longer loaded twice

> _2026-09-19 · core/blong-gogo · active_

Fixed by recording each realm's url inside loadRealm into a Set carried on the shared api: the
suite's children are realm *factories*, so the parent's wrapper could never read a url off them, and
the framework's frameworkRealms list therefore reloaded every realm a suite had already named (see
the friction entry). Impact to be aware of: each named framework realm was loaded twice, so every
handler group was registered twice and every subject.validation provider twice. Single-loading them
changes *registration order*, which is what made eight blong-access Playwright specs pass again: the
second blong-server copy had been registering server.subject.validation after the realm's explicit
gateway overrides (access.access.validation), so Registry._validations() replaced those overrides
with the auto schemas that require capabilityId/roleId/userId. Anything that depended on a doubled
registration - a portal contribution counted twice, a handlerCount of 2 - now behaves as one. The
snapshots that changed for this reason were regenerated deliberately.

### D-225 — Browser realms stay named in a suite's entry

> _2026-09-19 · core/blong-gogo · active_

Asked whether blong-suite/browser.ts could drop the references to blong the way server.ts does,
since the loader auto-includes the framework realms. It cannot, and the asymmetry is structural: the
server's auto-inclusion resolves each specifier at *runtime* from the suite's location
(createRequire), while a browser suite is bundled by Vite, which has to see the specifier in the
source it transforms - loadBrowser.ts's createRequire throws, resolveFromSuite swallows it and the
realm is skipped silently. A plugin, a virtual module or an import.meta.glob would each build the
edge at *build* time and were all rejected for the same reason: they only exist under Vite, so the
tap runner (which loads a browser suite through Node, where the loader *can* resolve) would see a
different graph. Owner decided to leave the browser entry as it is: it keeps one child function per
realm, with the config block and the unused validation entry dropped. Options if this is revisited:
a Vite-side injection in defineBlongViteConfig (framework-owned, invisible to suite authors) beside
the loader's runtime one.

### D-227 — Call records no longer depend on the component's log level

> _2026-09-19 · core/blong-gogo · active_

A consequence of moving the call records onto their own channel: they used to be written through
port.log.info, which a component above info simply does not have - a port configured at warn
produced no call records at all, silently, and the gateway's notes were only visible because
SemanticLog.child ignored its level option (fixed in the same session). Now the channel is
level-free by construction, so every component that records a call produces the record, and the two
realm baseline screenshots that show record-derived data (blong-template, blong-digest) changed for
that reason and were regenerated deliberately. The template page now shows the gateway's call-error
template with its context (gateway) and the error detail, which is what it showed before the
gateway's level stopped admitting info - so this restores the pre-existing picture rather than
inventing a new one. Anything reading record counts should expect more of them, not different ones:
the templates are the same set.

### D-228 — The embedder's log is held by the runtime, not extended by it

> _2026-09-19 · core/blong-gogo · active_

semantic-log's LogBase owns the emitter's construction, one logger per component, retention, the
cluster sink and init/stop. blong cannot extend it: load.ts decides a module is a component by
testing 'prototype instanceof Internal', and semantic-log knows nothing of Internal (nor should it).
So SemanticLog still extends Internal and *holds* a LogBase, and the two hooks it would otherwise
override are LogBaseOptions: 'envelope' (the $meta a call record carries) and 'translate' (reading
$meta out of a call site's arguments). Reconsidering this means changing that detection or marking
the class with system() - not changing the base.

### D-231 — What stayed in blong, and why the boundary is where it is

> _2026-09-19 · core/blong-gogo · active_

After the move, blong keeps: the $meta envelope (records and call sites), the binds-downwards
logger() contract and ILog's shapes, the call gate (callTrace.ts: config, opt-out patterns, blong
grant), resolveHome/thresholdOf (pino vocabulary). semantic-log owns: LogBase (construction,
per-component loggers, retention store, call-channel plumbing, cluster sink, init/stop), the pino
dialect (logCall.ts), the call channel (capability.ts), the service's start and cluster opener, and
the attachable facade. Two things stayed that a reader may expect to have moved: blong's pino Log
(it writes through pino transports, so the package owns nothing of it) and semanticContext.ts's
identity/leg/participant logic (~250 lines) - that is the framework's dispatch vocabulary, not the
emitter's.

### D-233 — Colour is decided by the intent rather than by the file descriptor

> _2026-09-19 · core/blong-gogo · active_

Playwright starts the backend with stdout piped, so isTTY() is false and the dev block left the
records plain - while the runner relays those same lines into the terminal and colours its own
output beside them. A piped stdout is therefore not evidence that nobody is watching. The playwright
intent now sets log.color true, and a new ci intent (which the same webServer passes last when CI is
set) sets it false again for a run whose output is captured. Verified on the gateway suite: 99 ANSI
escapes in the runners log lines, 0 with the ci intent, and the tap runner passes neither intent so
its plain output is unchanged.
